dedupe_keys.name: predicting wind damage to urban trees from first responder reports noord brabant knmi

description: KNMI researchers used ten years (2013 to 2023) of locations where emergency services recorded wind damage to public or private property, supplied by two safety regions in the Dutch province of Noord-Brabant, to predict where wind damage to urban trees and property is likely. Each report was enriched with weather and environmental features describing local conditions, and an ensemble of data-driven methods, one-class support vector machines, learned from these conditions and predicted for the rest of the study area. Coverage: Noord-Brabant, the Netherlands. Access: open-access article in Frontiers in Climate (December 2024). Licence: CC-BY-4.0 article. Caveats: the emergency-service reports themselves are not published with the article, and reports reflect where damage was called in, not a full damage census. Outcome: the ensemble mapped likely damage locations at 1 km and 5 km resolution under high and low wind scenarios, which the authors present as a step from hazard forecasts to impact-based forecasts and warnings. Simulation uses: impact-based warning, pre-positioning of emergency crews, and tree-fall risk layers for road and power networks. Related records: the Tongji street-tree wind fragility model and the urban forest storm data protocol.

name: Predicting wind damage to urban trees from first-responder reports, Noord-Brabant (KNMI)

outcomes: The data-driven ensemble learned from hyper-local conditions and mapped locations where wind damage is likely at 1 km and 5 km resolution under high and low wind scenarios, supporting KNMI's move toward impact-based warnings at urban scale.
